chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washa', from Hammad ibn Uthman, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying:
Ali (peace be upon him) used to allow, regarding debt, the testimony of one man and the oath of the claimant.

key_terms.الدَّيْنُ: dayn — debt or financial obligation; distinct from 'ariya (loan of object)
key_terms.الْمُدَّعِي: al-mudda'i — the claimant/plaintiff; the party making the financial claim
key_terms.شَهَادَة: shahada — legal testimony; here the testimony of one man (half the normal two-witness requirement)
key_terms.يَمِين: yamin — sworn oath; the claimant's oath supplements the single witness to complete proof

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali rule about one witness and an oath in debt cases according to Al-Kafi?
ai.summary: This hadith records Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) transmitting a judicial practice of Imam Ali (AS): in debt disputes, a single male witness combined with the claimant's sworn oath constitutes sufficient proof. This ruling addresses the frequent practical difficulty of gathering two full witnesses for financial claims, offering a more accessible evidentiary standard. For the Shia jurisprudential tradition, this practice attributed to Ali (AS) carries the weight of authoritative precedent from the first Imam and Commander of the Faithful.

en.hubeali: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moala Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Al Washa, from Hammad Bin Usman who said,
‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> Saying; ‘Ali<sup>asws</sup> used to allow, with regards to the debt, the testimony of a man and an oath of the claimant’.
en.sarwar: 1. Al-Husayn Muhammad has narrated from Mu‘alla’ ibn Muhammad from al-Hassan ibn Ali al-Washsha’ from Hammad ibn ‘Uthaman who has narrated the following: “I once heard abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saying
that in the case of a loan ’ Amir al-Mu’minin, Ali, Alayhi al-Salam, would accept the testimony of one person with the oath of the plaintiff.”’
